items.description: A substantial 367.3 g unclassified specimen with a rounded dark exterior and exposed weathered interior areas. Classification and find locality have not been recorded.
items.imageAlt: Three-quarter view of a rounded dark 367.3 g unclassified meteorite with a broad weathered interior exposure
items.name: Unclassified Meteorite

items.description: A 63.2 g Wabar related artifact showing black impact glass fused to pale desert sand. This is cataloged as terrestrial impact material, not as a meteorite.
items.imageAlt: Broad view of 63.2 g Wabar impact material with black glass fused over pale desert sand
items.name: Wabar Impact Glass with Fused Sand

items.description: A 30.4 g fragment of pale Wabar sand fused by impact heat, with layered texture and small dark glassy areas. Cataloged as impact material rather than a meteorite.
items.imageAlt: Front face of a pale 30.4 g Wabar impact-fused sand fragment
items.name: Wabar Impact-Fused Sand

items.description: A 7.9 g Wabar impact fragment combining dark glass, fused sand, and a remnant interpreted as relic meteoritic iron.
items.imageAlt: Wabar impact glass fragment with fused sand and relic iron
items.name: Wabar Impact Glass with Relic Iron

items.description: A small 0.7 g polished Wabar pearl with a glossy black surface and rounded oval form.
items.imageAlt: Front view of a polished black 0.7 g Wabar pearl
items.name: Wabar Pearl

items.description: A thin, angular 36.4 g iron fragment with a weathered metallic surface. Kaalijarv is an officially recognized IAB-MG iron meteorite found in Estonia in 1937; the Meteoritical Bulletin Database records 2.25 kg for the meteorite (code 12217).
items.imageAlt: Upright view of a thin angular 36.4 g Kaalijarv iron fragment with layered metallic texture
items.name: Kaalijarv

items.description: A 57.6 g cut wedge displaying a speckled interior. Cataloged as an unclassified ordinary chondrite; no official pairing or find locality is asserted.
items.imageAlt: Cut speckled face of a 57.6 g unclassified ordinary chondrite wedge
items.name: Unclassified Ordinary Chondrite

items.description: A 47.4 g unclassified Northwest Africa ordinary chondrite with a rounded, shield-like oriented form and visible surface cracking. No official pairing is asserted.
items.imageAlt: Shield-like face of a 47.4 g oriented Northwest Africa ordinary chondrite with branching surface cracks
items.name: Unclassified NWA Oriented Ordinary Chondrite

items.description: A historic 14 g Bjurböle collection fragment with a gray brecciated surface and the visible specimen marking OCH 238. Bjurböle is an officially recognized L/LL4 ordinary chondrite that fell in Uusimaa, Finland, in 1899; the Meteoritical Bulletin Database records 330 kg for the meteorite (code 5064).
items.imageAlt: Marked face of the historic 14 g Bjurböle L/LL4 fragment
items.name: Bjurböle

items.description: A large unclassified Northwest Africa ordinary chondrite with a broad weathered exterior, pronounced sculpting, and visible cracking. No official pairing is asserted.
items.imageAlt: Large 13.8 kg unclassified Northwest Africa ordinary chondrite
items.name: Large Unclassified NWA Ordinary Chondrite

items.description: Ksar Ghilane 022 is an officially recognized ungrouped achondrite found in Tatawin, Tunisia, in 2023 and described in the Meteoritical Bulletin as an Mg-rich clinopyroxenite composed predominantly of augite. This 31.35 g polished end cut displays a pale gray granular face crossed by a darker network and is held in the permanent collection (code 82150).
items.imageAlt: Polished face of the 31.35 g Ksar Ghilane 022 ungrouped achondrite with pale gray angular grains crossed by a dark network beside a scale cube
items.name: Ksar Ghilane 022
